item.text: The current helper keys entries by a reflected type name after stripping a leading `*`. That merges `T` and `*T`, which conflicts with the new API’s requirement for independent instances. I’m checking callers and the existing concurrency test before finishing the diagnosis.

Diagnosis: utils/singleton/singleton.go exposes only Get(object interface{}, constructor func() interface{}) interface{}. Its key is reflect.TypeOf(object).String() with a leading '*' removed, so value and pointer types collide. The serialized channel loop provides once-only construction for existing Get calls, but GetInstance[ T ] needs a key derived from T itself that preserves pointer depth and package identity, plus typed return semantics. Existing tests cover legacy Get, including 2,000 concurrent calls; no generic API or 20,000-call coverage. Source/tests untouched.
EOF"

item.text:
The fault is in [singleton.go](/app/utils/singleton/singleton.go:23): `Get` requires a placeholder and returns `interface{}`. Its cache key also strips `*` from the type name, so `T` and `*T` share an entry.

A fix should add `GetInstance[T any](constructor func() T) T`, key its cache by the exact `reflect.Type` of `T`, and synchronize the lookup and construction so concurrent callers receive one instance. Keep the existing `Get` behavior separate: [its tests](/app/utils/singleton/singleton_test.go:42) explicitly expect value and pointer placeholders to share an entry.

The existing tests pass, but cover only `Get` and 2,000 concurrent calls. They provide no evidence yet for the new generic API or the required 20,000-call case. Project source and tests were not changed, as required by the fault-localization assignment.
